pages.text: "All brushed!" Ppino the rabbit, always first at everything, rubbed the toothbrush twice and hung it on a wall peg. The morning bell had just rung. Corn hung in rows under the lodge eaves.
"They're boiling that corn tonight!" Ppino's ears leaned forward first. "I'll take the biggest bite!" Grandma Bear smiled and hung up another ear of corn.
At midday, they were in the wild raspberry patch. Ppino put a handful of bright red berries in their mouth. Chew, chew. Their cheeks reddened. One seed stuck between the front teeth.
The dinner bell rang, and corn came to the long table. Ppino lifted the biggest ear and took a wide bite. But the front teeth prickled and tingled!
Ppino set the corn back down. Rudi was already eating a second ear. "Only I can't eat..." Ppino's ears drooped.
Grandma Bear sat in front of Ppino and looked at their face. "Could you show me your front teeth?" "Aaah." One dark seed sat between them.
Grandma took Ppino's brush from its peg. Side by side, they brushed. Front teeth, brush, brush. Inside, brush, brush. Even the back teeth, brush, brush! "Front teeth, inside—brush, brush!"
Ppino took water into their mouth and spat. The dark seed dropped into the wooden bowl. Between the front teeth, all smooth. Ppino took a big bite of the corn left over.
The next morning, Ppino took their brush down first. "One, front teeth, brush, brush! Two, inside, brush, brush! Three, back teeth too, brush, brush!" Rudi took their brush from the next peg.

Grandma touched her nose gently to Ppino's. "Teeth white as snow." Two quick brushes leave a seed behind; brush everywhere, and corn tastes good. "Front teeth, inside—brush, brush!" Ppino smiled, showing their teeth.
